No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote or pre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. For geographically dispersed populations, such as West Point and Senior ROTC Cadets who matriculate across hundreds of universities without visiting a MEPS facility, 3 there is no standardized mechanism to collect pre-arrival sizing data. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boot

tact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommended standard Army

ughput: Batch processing at MEPS and IET Reception facilities. o Remote Self-Assessment: A mobile self-service assessment accessible via standard smart devices for geographically dispersed individuals. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats.
